JavaScript

const canvas = document.querySelector('#map');
const ACCENT = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--accent').trim();
let progress = 0.4;

// The route: a cubic Bézier curve in 0–1 units, scaled to the canvas size
const P = [[0.08, 0.75], [0.35, 0.02], [0.62, 1.1], [0.9, 0.3]];
function pointAt(t, w, h) {
  const u = 1 - t;
  const k = [u ** 3, 3 * u * u * t, 3 * u * t * t, t ** 3];
  return [0, 1].map((axis) => k.reduce((s, c, i) => s + c * P[i][axis], 0) * (axis ? h : w));
}

function setup() {
  const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
  const { width, height } = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
  canvas.width = Math.round(width * dpr);           // backing store in device pixels
  canvas.height = Math.round(height * dpr);
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);            // now 1 unit = 1 CSS pixel
  return { ctx, w: width, h: height, dpr };
}

function label(ctx, text, x, y, maxX) {
  ctx.font = '600 12px system-ui, sans-serif';
  const w = ctx.measureText(text).width + 16;
  x = Math.min(Math.max(x, w / 2 + 6), maxX - w / 2 - 6);   // keep it inside
  ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#ddd6fe';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.roundRect(x - w / 2, y - 34, w, 22, 11);
  ctx.fill();
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#1e1b3a';
  ctx.textAlign = 'center';
  ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
  ctx.fillText(text, x, y - 23);
}

function draw() {
  const { ctx, w, h, dpr } = setup();
  // 1. Rectangles and straight lines: the map
  ctx.fillStyle = '#faf9ff';
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h);
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#efecfb';
  ctx.lineWidth = 8;
  for (let x = 30; x < w; x += 110) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, 0); ctx.lineTo(x + 40, h); ctx.stroke();
  }
  for (let y = 40; y < h; y += 70) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, y); ctx.lineTo(w, y - 16); ctx.stroke();
  }
  // 2. A curved path: the full route, dashed
  const [sx, sy] = pointAt(0, w, h);
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(sx, sy);
  ctx.bezierCurveTo(P[1][0] * w, P[1][1] * h, P[2][0] * w, P[2][1] * h, P[3][0] * w, P[3][1] * h);
  ctx.setLineDash([2, 8]);
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  ctx.lineWidth = 4;
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#c4b5fd';
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  // 3. The distance travelled, sampled into a polyline
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (let i = 0; i <= 60; i++) ctx.lineTo(...pointAt((i / 60) * progress, w, h));
  ctx.lineWidth = 5;
  ctx.strokeStyle = ACCENT;
  ctx.stroke();
  // 4. Arcs: warehouse, home pin and rider
  const [ex, ey] = pointAt(1, w, h);
  const [rx, ry] = pointAt(progress, w, h);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#1e1b3a';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(sx, sy, 7, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#ef4444';
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(ex, ey - 16, 10, Math.PI * 0.8, Math.PI * 2.2);   // round top of the pin…
  ctx.lineTo(ex, ey);                                         // …down to its point
  ctx.closePath();
  ctx.fill();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ex, ey - 16, 4, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
  ctx.globalAlpha = 0.18;
  ctx.fillStyle = ACCENT;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(rx, ry, 18, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(rx, ry, 9, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
  ctx.lineWidth = 3;
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#fff';
  ctx.stroke();
  // 5. Text
  label(ctx, 'Ralfiz warehouse', sx, sy, w);
  label(ctx, 'Home', ex, ey - 14, w);
  document.querySelector('#info').textContent =
    `backing ${canvas.width}×${canvas.height} px · CSS ${Math.round(w)}×${h} · DPR ${dpr}`;
}

function update() {
  const mins = Math.round((1 - progress) * 24);
  const done = progress >= 1;
  document.querySelector('#eta').textContent = done ? 'Delivered' : `Arriving in ${mins} min`;
  document.querySelector('#status').textContent = done ? 'Delivered' : 'On the way';
  document.querySelector('#status').classList.toggle('done', done);
  canvas.setAttribute('aria-label', `Delivery map: the rider is ${Math.round(progress * 100)}% of the way to your home`);
  draw();
}

document.querySelector('#move').addEventListener('click', () => {
  progress = progress >= 1 ? 0.1 : Math.min(1, progress + 0.2);
  update();
  console.log('repainted at', Math.round(progress * 100) + '%');
});
new ResizeObserver(draw).observe(canvas);           // redraw when the width changes
update();

Press Move rider. Every press repaints the whole canvas: rectangles for the street grid, a dashed Bézier path for the route, arcs for the stops and the rider, and measured text for the labels.

Sharp drawing on high-density screens

Phones and many laptops have a devicePixelRatio of 2 or 3: one CSS pixel is 2 × 2 or 3 × 3 physical pixels. A 300 × 150 canvas shown at 300 × 150 CSS pixels on such a screen is stretched, so lines and text look soft. The fix is three lines: make the backing store bigger by the ratio, keep the CSS size, and scale the context so you still draw in CSS pixels.

function setupCanvas(canvas) {
  const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
  const { width, height } = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();  // CSS size
  canvas.width = Math.round(width * dpr);
  canvas.height = Math.round(height * dpr);
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);  // 1 unit = 1 CSS pixel
  return { ctx, width, height };
}

Use setTransform rather than scale: scale multiplies the current transform, so calling the setup twice would scale twice. Also note the .5 trick: a 1px line centred on a whole coordinate covers two half pixels and looks grey, so thin lines are drawn at x + 0.5. The page below simulates a 2× and 3× phone so you can see the difference even on a 1× monitor.

JavaScript

const W = 156;                 // CSS size of the drawing
const H = 56;
const naive = document.querySelector('#naive');
const sharp = document.querySelector('#sharp');

// The real-world helper: size the backing store, then draw in CSS pixels
function prepare(canvas, ratio) {
  canvas.width = Math.round(W * ratio);
  canvas.height = Math.round(H * ratio);
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.setTransform(ratio, 0, 0, ratio, 0, 0);
  return ctx;
}

function star(ctx, cx, cy, r) {
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    const radius = i % 2 ? r * 0.45 : r;
    const a = -Math.PI / 2 + (i * Math.PI) / 5;
    ctx.lineTo(cx + radius * Math.cos(a), cy + radius * Math.sin(a));
  }
  ctx.closePath();
  ctx.fill();
}

function drawTag(ctx) {
  ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#0f766e';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.roundRect(4.5, 8.5, 147, 39, 8);   // .5 puts a 1px line on a pixel row
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#f59e0b';
  star(ctx, 21, 28, 8);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#0f2e2a';
  ctx.font = '700 16px system-ui, sans-serif';
  ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
  ctx.fillText('₹2,499', 35, 28.5);
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#ccebe5';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(104.5, 16); ctx.lineTo(104.5, 40); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = '#dc2626';
  ctx.font = '600 11px system-ui, sans-serif';
  ctx.textAlign = 'center';
  ctx.fillText('−20%', 128, 28.5);
}

function render(zoom) {
  // Show both canvases magnified, like a zoom× screen would
  naive.style.width = sharp.style.width = W * zoom + 'px';
  drawTag(prepare(naive, 1));          // the usual first attempt
  drawTag(prepare(sharp, zoom));       // backing store matches the screen
  document.querySelector('#naiveInfo').textContent = `${naive.width}×${naive.height} bitmap, stretched ${zoom}×`;
  document.querySelector('#sharpInfo').textContent = `${sharp.width}×${sharp.height} bitmap, 1:1`;
  document.querySelector('#note').textContent =
    `Your screen: devicePixelRatio = ${devicePixelRatio}. Magnified ${zoom}× to show what a ${zoom}× phone displays.`;
  console.log(`zoom ${zoom}×: naive ${naive.width}×${naive.height}, sharp ${sharp.width}×${sharp.height}`);
}

document.querySelector('.seg').addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const btn = e.target.closest('[data-zoom]');
  if (!btn) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.seg button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b === btn)));
  render(Number(btn.dataset.zoom));
});
render(2);

Both tags are drawn with the same code at 156×56 CSS pixels, then shown magnified the way a 2× or 3× phone screen displays them. Only the right one sized its backing store by the pixel ratio.

Drawing a bar chart from data

A chart is just arithmetic that maps data to pixels, called a scale. Pick a “nice” maximum that splits into round steps (a best month of ₹8.18L gives an axis up to ₹10L with grid lines every ₹2.5L), then y(v) = bottom - (v / max) * plotHeight. Split the width into one slot per month, and draw each bar inside its slot with some padding. Draw grid lines and labels first so the bars sit on top.

Because canvas keeps no objects, interaction is your job. event.target is always the canvas. Save the rectangles you drew in an array, convert the pointer position with event.clientX - canvas.getBoundingClientRect().left (CSS pixels, the same units you drew in thanks to setTransform), and find the bar under it. This is called hit testing.

When the layout width changes, the backing store must change too, so observe the canvas with a ResizeObserver (dm14), re-run the setup and redraw. Reading colours from CSS custom properties with getComputedStyle keeps the chart in step with your theme.

JavaScript

const MONTHS = ['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec', 'Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar'];
const DATA = {
  'FY 2025–26': [412000, 388000, 505000, 462000, 590000, 638000, 571000, 684000, 731000, 652000, 704000, 818000],
  'FY 2024–25': [305000, 296000, 352000, 341000, 402000, 455000, 498000, 560000, 612000, 488000, 515000, 590000],
};
const canvas = document.querySelector('#chart');
const tip = document.querySelector('#tip');
const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
const color = (name) => css.getPropertyValue(name).trim();   // share colours with CSS
const inr = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR', maximumFractionDigits: 0 });
const lakh = (v) => '₹' + +(v / 1e5).toFixed(1) + 'L';
const reduce = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');

let fy = 'FY 2025–26';
let shown = MONTHS.map(() => 0);   // bar values as currently drawn
let bars = [];                     // hit boxes from the last draw
let hover = -1;
let ctx, W, H, frame = 0;

function resize() {                // only when the size changes
  const dpr = devicePixelRatio || 1;
  ({ width: W, height: H } = canvas.getBoundingClientRect());
  canvas.width = Math.round(W * dpr);
  canvas.height = Math.round(H * dpr);
  ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
  draw();
}

// A round maximum that splits into 4 steps of 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 × 10ⁿ
function niceMax(v) {
  const raw = v / 4;
  const p = 10 ** Math.floor(Math.log10(raw));
  const m = [1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10].find((n) => n * p >= raw);
  return 4 * m * p;
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);       // canvas remembers nothing: clear, then paint all
  const pad = { top: 12, right: 4, bottom: 24, left: 44 };
  const plotH = H - pad.top - pad.bottom;
  const base = pad.top + plotH;
  const max = niceMax(Math.max(...DATA[fy]));
  const y = (v) => base - (v / max) * plotH;
  ctx.font = '11px system-ui, sans-serif';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i <= 4; i++) {
    const gy = Math.round(y((max / 4) * i)) + 0.5;
    ctx.strokeStyle = color(i ? '--grid' : '--axis');
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(pad.left, gy); ctx.lineTo(W - pad.right, gy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = color('--muted');
    ctx.textAlign = 'right';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.fillText(i ? lakh((max / 4) * i) : '₹0', pad.left - 8, gy);
  }
  const slot = (W - pad.left - pad.right) / shown.length;
  const bw = Math.min(34, slot * 0.62);
  bars = shown.map((v, i) => {
    const x = pad.left + slot * i + (slot - bw) / 2;
    const top = y(v);
    ctx.fillStyle = color(i === hover ? '--accent-strong' : '--accent');
    ctx.globalAlpha = hover === -1 || i === hover ? 1 : 0.45;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.roundRect(x, top, bw, base - top, [6, 6, 0, 0]);
    ctx.fill();
    ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
    ctx.fillStyle = color('--muted');
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'top';
    ctx.fillText(slot < 34 ? MONTHS[i][0] : MONTHS[i], x + bw / 2, base + 8);   // narrow: J F M
    return { x: pad.left + slot * i, w: slot, top, mid: x + bw / 2 };
  });
}

function animateTo(target) {
  cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
  const from = shown.slice();
  if (reduce.matches) { shown = target.slice(); draw(); return; }
  let start = null;
  const step = (now) => {
    start ??= now;
    const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / 700);
    const e = 1 - (1 - t) ** 3;                         // ease-out
    shown = from.map((f, i) => f + (target[i] - f) * e);
    draw();
    if (t < 1) frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    else console.log(`${fy}: 12 bars · ${Math.round(W)}×${H} CSS px · DPR ${devicePixelRatio}`);
  };
  frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
}

function show(name) {
  fy = name;
  const values = DATA[fy];
  const total = values.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const best = values.indexOf(Math.max(...values));
  document.querySelector('#total').textContent = inr.format(total);
  document.querySelector('#sub').textContent = `${fy} · best month ${MONTHS[best]} (${lakh(values[best])})`;
  canvas.setAttribute('aria-label', `Monthly revenue ${fy}: from ${lakh(values[0])} in April to ${lakh(values[11])} in March, total ${inr.format(total)}`);
  animateTo(values);
}

canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  const x = e.clientX - canvas.getBoundingClientRect().left;  // CSS pixels, like our drawing
  const i = bars.findIndex((b) => x >= b.x && x < b.x + b.w);
  if (i !== hover) { hover = i; draw(); }
  tip.hidden = i < 0;
  if (i < 0) return;
  tip.innerHTML = '<b></b><span></span>';
  tip.querySelector('b').textContent = inr.format(DATA[fy][i]);
  tip.querySelector('span').textContent = MONTHS[i] + ' · ' + fy;
  tip.style.left = Math.min(W - 70, Math.max(70, bars[i].mid)) + 'px';
  tip.style.top = bars[i].top + 'px';
});
canvas.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { hover = -1; tip.hidden = true; draw(); });

document.querySelector('.seg').addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const btn = e.target.closest('[data-fy]');
  if (!btn) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.seg button').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b === btn)));
  show(btn.dataset.fy);
});

resize();
new ResizeObserver(resize).observe(canvas);
show(fy);

Simple animation on canvas

Canvas animation is the rAF loop from dm15 with one rule: each frame clears and repaints the whole scene from state. To animate bars, store the values currently shown, and on each frame move them towards the target by an eased fraction of the elapsed time:

function animateTo(target, duration = 700) {
  cancelAnimationFrame(frame);             // never run two loops
  const from = shown.slice();
  let start = null;
  const step = (now) => {
    start ??= now;
    const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / duration);
    const e = 1 - (1 - t) ** 3;            // ease-out
    shown = from.map((f, i) => f + (target[i] - f) * e);
    draw();                                // clearRect + paint everything
    if (t < 1) frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  };
  frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
}

Resize the backing store only when the size changes, never on every frame: setting canvas.width reallocates memory. And when prefers-reduced-motion matches, draw the final state at once.

Inline SVG with createElementNS

SVG elements live in their own XML namespace. In an HTML document, document.createElement('circle') creates an unknown HTML element that draws nothing. Always use createElementNS, and set geometry with setAttribute, because SVG properties such as circle.r are read-only animated objects, not plain numbers.

const NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
function svg(tag, attrs = {}, ...children) {
  const el = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) el.setAttribute(k, v);
  el.append(...children);
  return el;
}

// A crisp icon that follows the text colour
const chevron = svg('svg', { viewBox: '0 0 24 24', width: 16, height: 16,
  fill: 'none', stroke: 'currentColor', 'stroke-width': 2, 'aria-hidden': 'true' },
  svg('path', { d: 'm9 18 6-6-6-6' }));
button.append(chevron);

viewBox defines the internal coordinates, so the same icon is sharp at 16px or 160px. stroke="currentColor" makes it inherit the CSS color, so hover styles and dark mode just work. Decorative icons get aria-hidden="true"; a meaningful graphic gets role="img" and a <title> or aria-label.

An SVG donut chart

A donut is a set of circles with a thick stroke. The trick is stroke-dasharray: with circumference C = 2πr, a dash of share × C followed by a long gap draws one arc, and stroke-dashoffset shifts it to start after the previous segment. Rotate the group by -90° so the first segment starts at 12 o’clock. Because each segment is an element, it gets real pointerenter and focus events, a tooltip via <title>, and CSS transitions for free.

const R = 70;
const C = 2 * Math.PI * R;          // circumference: the length of one full stroke
const chart = svg('svg', { viewBox: '0 0 200 200', role: 'img', 'aria-labelledby': 'donut-title' },
  svg('title', { id: 'donut-title' }, 'Sales by category'),

const segs = CATS.map((c, i) => svg('circle', { cx: 100, cy: 100, r: R, stroke: c.color,
  class: 'seg-arc', tabindex: 0, 'data-i': i }, svg('title')));
ring.append(...segs);
chart.append(ring, big, small);
document.querySelector('#donut').append(chart);

const legend = document.querySelector('#legend');
const rows = CATS.map((c, i) => {
  const li = document.createElement('li');
  li.dataset.i = i;
  li.innerHTML = '<span class="dot"></span><span></span><span class="val"></span><span class="pct"></span>';
  li.firstChild.style.background = c.color;
  li.children[1].textContent = c.name;
  return li;
});
legend.append(...rows);

const total = () => CATS.reduce((s, c) => s + c[measure], 0);
function centre(i) {
  const c = CATS[i];
  big.textContent = fmt[measure](c ? c[measure] : total());
  small.textContent = c ? c.name : measure === 'revenue' ? 'total revenue' : 'total orders';

function render() {
  const sum = total();
  let offset = 0;
  CATS.forEach((c, i) => {
    const len = (c[measure] / sum) * C;
    segs[i].style.strokeDasharray = `${Math.max(0, len - 2)} ${C}`;   // dash, then a long gap
    segs[i].style.strokeDashoffset = -offset;                         // start after the previous one
    offset += len;
    const pct = Math.round((c[measure] / sum) * 100) + '%';
    segs[i].firstChild.textContent = `${c.name}: ${fmt[measure](c[measure])} (${pct})`;
    rows[i].querySelector('.val').textContent = fmt[measure](c[measure]);
    rows[i].querySelector('.pct').textContent = pct;

for (const el of [...segs, ...rows]) {
  const i = Number(el.dataset.i);
  el.addEventListener('pointerenter', () => highlight(i));
  el.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => highlight(-1));
  el.addEventListener('focus', () => highlight(i));
  el.addEventListener('blur', () => highlight(-1));
}

Canvas vs SVG vs plain DOM

CanvasSVGHTML + CSS
ModelPixels, redraw everythingVector elements in the DOMBoxes and text in the DOM
Best forThousands of points, games, image editing, heatmapsCharts with tens to a few thousand shapes, icons, logos, diagramsProgress bars, simple bar lists, layout, text-heavy UI
Events and hit testingManualPer elementPer element
AccessibilityNeeds a label and a text alternativetitle, role, aria-*, focusableNative semantics
SharpnessNeeds devicePixelRatio handlingAlways sharpAlways sharp
Cost grows withPixels drawnNumber of elementsNumber of elements
Remember: start with HTML and CSS. A horizontal bar list is a few divs with a width. Move to SVG when you need curves or arcs, and to canvas when element counts or per-pixel work make the DOM slow.

Common mistakes

  • Sizing a canvas only with CSS. 
    // Wrong: a 300 × 150 bitmap stretched to fill the card
canvas.style.width = '100%';
// Right: backing store = CSS size × devicePixelRatio
const { width, height } = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
canvas.width = width * devicePixelRatio;
canvas.height = height * devicePixelRatio;
ctx.setTransform(devicePixelRatio, 0, 0, devicePixelRatio, 0, 0);
  • Forgetting beginPath(). Every new shape is added to the old path, so each fill() repaints all earlier shapes in the new colour. 
    // Wrong: the second fill also recolours the first circle
ctx.arc(50, 50, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fillStyle = 'red'; ctx.fill();
ctx.arc(90, 50, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fillStyle = 'blue'; ctx.fill();
// Right: one path per shape
ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(90, 50, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
  • Creating SVG with createElement or setting properties. 
    // Wrong: an HTML element, and r is a read-only SVGAnimatedLength
const c = document.createElement('circle');
c.r = 10;
// Right
const c = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
c.setAttribute('r', 10);
  • Animating without clearing. Each frame paints on top of the last one, leaving trails. 
    // Wrong
function frame() { drawBars(shown); requestAnimationFrame(frame); }
// Right
function frame() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);
  drawBars(shown);
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
  • A chart nobody can read without eyes. 
    <!-- Wrong: a blank box for screen readers -->
<canvas id="chart"></canvas>
<!-- Right: a name that states the insight, plus the data as text nearby -->
<canvas id="chart" role="img"
  aria-label="Revenue grew from ₹4.1L in April to ₹8.2L in March"></canvas>

Interview and real-world notes

  • “Canvas or SVG?” Explain immediate vs retained mode, then decide by element count, need for events and accessibility, and pixel effects. Mention that plain HTML and CSS is often enough.
  • “Why is my canvas blurry?” Backing store vs CSS size and devicePixelRatio; use setTransform so the setup is idempotent.
  • Performance: redraw only on change or inside one rAF loop; for heavy work, OffscreenCanvas can render in a Web Worker (check caniuse.com). For large SVGs, fewer elements and CSS transform animations keep things smooth.
  • Libraries: Chart.js draws on canvas, D3 usually produces SVG. Knowing the underlying API makes debugging them far easier.
  • Security: never build SVG markup from user data with innerHTML: SVG can carry scripts and event handlers. Create elements and set textContent, as in this lesson.

  1. C. A canvas defaults to 300 × 150, and colours are read back as hex. Setting width (even to the same value) clears the bitmap and resets the whole context state, so fillStyle and lineWidth return to their defaults.
  2. A. createElement makes an HTML element (an unknown one, with an upper-case tagName). Only createElementNS with the SVG namespace makes a real SVG circle, whose tagName keeps its case.

terms.definition: The object returned by canvas.getContext('2d'). It holds drawing state (fillStyle, lineWidth, font, transform) and methods such as fillRect, arc and fillText.
The real pixel grid of a canvas, set by its width and height attributes. Its CSS size only controls how big that bitmap is displayed.
How many physical screen pixels make one CSS pixel: 1 on many laptops, 2 or 3 on phones. Multiply the backing store by it for sharp drawing.
A list of lines and curves started with beginPath(), built with moveTo, lineTo, arc or bezierCurveTo, then painted with fill() or stroke().
Canvas is immediate mode: pixels are painted and forgotten. SVG and the DOM are retained mode: the browser keeps objects you can change later.
Creates an element in a given namespace. SVG needs 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', otherwise you get an unknown HTML element that draws nothing.
The SVG attribute that sets the internal coordinate system (min-x, min-y, width, height), so the drawing scales to any displayed size.

quiz.explanation: Canvas cost depends on pixels, not on the number of objects kept in the DOM. 50,000 SVG or DOM nodes would make style, layout and hit testing slow.

quiz.question: On a canvas, the user hovers over a bar. How do you know which bar it is?
options: event.target is the bar element
Call canvas.querySelector on the bar
Canvas shapes fire their own pointerenter events
Keep the bar rectangles from your last draw and test the pointer position against them
quiz.explanation: Canvas keeps no objects, so event.target is always the canvas. You store the geometry you drew and do your own hit testing with the pointer coordinates.

lessons.title: More web platform APIs
lessons.summaryHtml:
The browser is more than a document viewer: it gives your page access to the clipboard, the system share sheet, the user’s colour scheme, the network state, notifications and location. These web platform APIs turn a static page into something that feels like a native app.

They share three rules. Many only work in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost). The powerful ones need a user gesture such as a click, and some ask for permission through a browser prompt. Support differs between browsers, so you always use feature detection and give a fallback.

In this lesson you build a copy-to-clipboard coupon, a theme that follows the system, and an online/offline status panel, and you see the code for notifications and geolocation.
lessons.contentHtml:
In plain words

So far you have used the DOM to change what is on the page. The browser also exposes a set of device and system features to JavaScript: the clipboard, the share sheet you know from your phone, the user’s dark-mode setting, whether the network is up, whether the tab is visible, desktop notifications and the device location. Each one is a small API on navigator, document or window.

Think of them as doors in a building. Some are open to everyone (matchMedia). Some open only when a person is standing there pressing the handle (a user gesture, such as a click). Some need a key from the owner (a permission prompt). And some doors only exist in newer buildings, so you check that the door is there before you walk into it (feature detection).

Why it matters

Small touches like these separate a professional product from a student project. A “Copy code” button on a coupon saves the user from long-pressing tiny text. A Share button opens WhatsApp or Mail directly on a phone. A dashboard that turns dark with the operating system feels native. A notes app that says “You are offline, changes will sync later” prevents lost work and angry support tickets.

They also come up in real bugs. A share button that throws on desktop Firefox, a clipboard call that silently fails inside an iframe, a timer that runs wrong in a background tab, or a location request on page load that users deny forever: all of these are shipped by developers who did not know the rules below.

How it works

The three rules: secure context, user activation, permission

Browsers protect users by putting powerful features behind gates. Learn the gates once and every API makes sense.

APISecure contextUser gesturePermission prompt
matchMediaNoNoNo
Page Visibility, navigator.onLineNoNoNo
navigator.clipboard.writeTextYesUsually (varies by browser)No for writing
navigator.clipboard.readTextYesYesYes, or a paste button
navigator.shareYesYesNo (the share sheet is the confirmation)
NotificationsYesNeeded for the prompt in most browsersYes
GeolocationYesRecommendedYes

A secure context means HTTPS or http://localhost, which is why Live Server works for these labs. There is a fourth gate for embedded pages: Permissions Policy. An iframe only gets features such as clipboard-write or geolocation if the parent page allows them, for example <iframe allow="clipboard-write">. The playground frame on this site does not, which is useful: you will see the fallback paths run.

Feature detection, not browser detection

Never check the browser name in the user agent string: it lies, and it goes stale. Check for the thing you want to use. If navigator.share is a function, show a Share button; if not, show Copy link. This is progressive enhancement: the base experience works everywhere and better APIs add to it. CSS.supports() does the same job for CSS features, and navigator.permissions.query() tells you whether a permission is granted, denied or prompt without showing a prompt.

Try it: Feature detection report

JavaScript

const features = {
  secureContext: window.isSecureContext,
  clipboardWrite: typeof navigator.clipboard?.writeText === 'function',
  webShare: typeof navigator.share === 'function',
  notifications: 'Notification' in window,
  geolocation: 'geolocation' in navigator,
  permissionsApi: 'permissions' in navigator,
  vibrate: 'vibrate' in navigator,
};
console.table(features);

// Decide the UI from the result, never from the browser name
console.log(features.webShare
  ? 'Show the native Share button'
  : 'Hide Share, offer Copy link instead');

// CSS features can be detected too
console.log('CSS :has() support:', CSS.supports('selector(:has(a))'));
console.log('Prefers dark:', matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches);

// Ask about a permission WITHOUT showing a prompt
if (navigator.permissions) {
  navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'geolocation' })
    .then((status) => console.log('geolocation permission:', status.state))
    .catch((err) => console.warn('Cannot query:', err.name));
}

Run this and compare with your own browser tab: the playground frame is sandboxed, so some features are present but not allowed.

Remember: an API existing is not the same as it being allowed. navigator.clipboard can exist while a call still rejects with NotAllowedError. Feature-detect and handle the rejection.

Clipboard API: copy on click

navigator.clipboard.writeText(text) returns a promise. It resolves when the text is on the clipboard and rejects if the browser refuses, for example because the page is not focused, there was no recent click, or a Permissions Policy blocks it. Call it inside the click handler, await it, and only then say “Copied”. If it fails, a friendly fallback is to select the text in an input so the user can press Ctrl+C. You may see the old document.execCommand('copy') in tutorials: it is deprecated, so treat it as legacy only.

Try it: Copy-to-clipboard coupon

HTML

<main class="deal">
  <header class="top">
    <span class="logo">R</span><strong>Ralfiz Store</strong>
    <span class="pill">Festive sale</span>
  </header>
  <section class="card">
    <div class="art" aria-hidden="true">🎧</div>
    <div class="body">
      <p class="eyebrow">Limited offer · ends Sunday</p>
      <h1>Flat 20% off all headphones</h1>
      <p class="muted">Apply this code at checkout. One use per account.</p>
      <div class="code-row">
        <input id="code" value="RALFIZ20" readonly aria-label="Coupon code">
        <button id="copy" class="btn primary" type="button">Copy code</button>
      </div>
      <button id="share" class="btn ghost" type="button">↗ Share this deal</button>
      <p id="status" class="status" role="status"></p>
    </div>
  </section>
</main>

CSS

.deal { max-width: 560px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; }

  color: #fff; display: grid; place-items: center; font-weight: 700; }
.pill { margin-left: auto; font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 99px;
  background: #eef2ff; color: var(--accent); font-weight: 600; }
.card { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; background: #fff;
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px;
  box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(17, 24, 39, .06); }
.art { flex: 0 0 96px; height: 96px; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 48px;
  display: grid; place-items: center;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #eef2ff, #fce7f3); }
.body { flex: 1 1 260px; min-width: 0; }
.eyebrow { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: #db2777;
  text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .04em; }
h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 4px 0; }
.muted { color: var(--muted); margin: 0 0 12px; font-size: 14px; }
.code-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
#code { flex: 1; min-width: 0; font: 600 16px ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace;
  letter-spacing: .12em; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 10px;
  border: 1.5px dashed #a5b4fc; background: #f8f9ff; color: #312e81; }
#code:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.btn { font: inherit; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 14px;
  cursor: pointer; border: 1px solid transparent; }
.primary { background: var(--accent); color: #fff; }
.primary:hover { background: #4338ca; }
.ghost { background: #fff; border-color: var(--line); color: #374151; width: 100%; }
.ghost:hover { background: #f9fafb; }
.btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.status { min-height: 20px; margin: 8px 0 0; font-size: 13px; color: #047857; }
.status[data-tone="info"] { color: #1d4ed8; }

JavaScript

const codeInput = document.querySelector('#code');
const copyBtn = document.querySelector('#copy');
const shareBtn = document.querySelector('#share');
const statusEl = document.querySelector('#status');

function say(message, tone = 'ok') {
  statusEl.textContent = message;
  statusEl.dataset.tone = tone;
}

// Returns 'copied' or 'selected' so the caller can word the message
async function copyText(text) {
  if (navigator.clipboard?.writeText) {
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      return 'copied';
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('Clipboard write refused:', err.name);
    }
  }
  codeInput.focus();
  codeInput.select(); // fallback: the user presses Ctrl+C
  return 'selected';
}

copyBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const result = await copyText(codeInput.value);
  if (result === 'copied') {
    copyBtn.textContent = 'Copied ✓';
    say('Code copied. Paste it at checkout.');
    setTimeout(() => { copyBtn.textContent = 'Copy code'; }, 2000);
  } else {
    say('Code selected: press Ctrl+C (⌘C on Mac) to copy it.', 'info');
  }
});

const deal = {
  title: 'Ralfiz Store deal',
  text: 'Flat 20% off headphones with code RALFIZ20',
  url: 'https://shop.ralfiz.dev/deals/headphones',
};

shareBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (navigator.share && navigator.canShare?.(deal) !== false) {
    try {
      await navigator.share(deal);
      say('Thanks for sharing!');
      return;
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.name === 'AbortError') return say('Share cancelled.', 'info');
      console.warn('Share failed:', err.name);
    }
  }
  const result = await copyText(deal.url);
  say(result === 'copied' ? 'Link copied instead.' : 'Sharing is not available here.', 'info');
});

console.log('Clipboard API:', Boolean(navigator.clipboard),
  '| Web Share:', typeof navigator.share === 'function');

Click Copy code. This frame has no clipboard permission, so you will see the fallback path: the code is selected and the user is told to press Ctrl+C.

Reading the clipboard (readText) is far more sensitive, because the clipboard may hold a password. Browsers show a prompt or a paste button, so only read when the user clearly asked, for example a “Paste OTP” button.

Web Share API: the native share sheet

navigator.share({ title, text, url }) opens the operating system’s share sheet, the same one a native app uses. It needs a secure context and a user gesture. The promise rejects with AbortError when the user closes the sheet, which is not a real error, so ignore it quietly. navigator.canShare(data) checks whether the data (for example files) can be shared. Support is strong on mobile browsers and Safari, and patchy on desktop, so always keep a Copy link fallback. Check the MDN compatibility table before you rely on it.

shareBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (!navigator.share) return copyLink(); // fallback
  try {
    await navigator.share({ title: 'Ralfiz Store', url: location.href });
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name !== 'AbortError') copyLink(); // user cancel is fine
  }
});

matchMedia: CSS media queries in JavaScript

matchMedia(query) returns a MediaQueryList. Its matches property answers the query right now, and its change event fires when the answer flips. Use it for (prefers-color-scheme: dark), (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and breakpoints such as (min-width: 560px). It is better than listening to resize for breakpoints, because it fires once when the line is crossed rather than dozens of times per second.

A good theme switcher has three choices: System, Light and Dark. The saved choice goes in localStorage; the actual theme is derived from the choice plus the media query. Set it as data-theme on the html element and let CSS custom properties do the rest. Set color-scheme too, so scrollbars and form controls match.

Try it: Theme that follows the system

HTML

<main class="shell">
  <header class="bar">
    <strong>Ralfiz Academy</strong>
    <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Theme">
      <button type="button" data-choice="system">System</button>
      <button type="button" data-choice="light">Light</button>
      <button type="button" data-choice="dark">Dark</button>
    </div>
  </header>
  <section class="grid">
    <article class="tile"><p class="k">Lessons done</p><p class="v">18 / 24</p>
      <div class="meter"><span style="width:75%"></span></div></article>
    <article class="tile"><p class="k">Streak</p><p class="v">🔥 9 days</p>
      <p class="hint">Keep it going tomorrow</p></article>
    <article class="tile"><p class="k">Your system prefers</p>
      <p class="v" id="sys">…</p><p class="hint" id="bp">…</p></article>
  </section>
</main>

CSS

:root { --bg: #f6f7fb; --card: #fff; --text: #111827; --muted: #6b7280;
  --line: #e5e7eb; --accent: #0d9488; color-scheme: light; }
:root[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0b1020; --card: #141a2e; --text: #e5e7eb;
  --muted: #9ca3af; --line: #26304a; --accent: #2dd4bf; color-scheme: dark; }
body { margin: 0; background: var(--bg); color: var(--text);
  transition: background .25s, color .25s; }
.shell { padding: 16px; max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; }
.bar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 16px; }
.seg { display: inline-flex; padding: 4px; gap: 4px; border-radius: 12px;
  background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.seg button { font: inherit; font-size: 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 6px 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--muted); cursor: pointer; }
.seg button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--accent); color: #fff; }
.seg button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.grid { display: grid; gap: 12px;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr)); }
.tile { background: var(--card); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 14px;
  padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, .05); }
.k { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: var(--muted); }
.v { margin: 4px 0 8px; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700; }
.hint { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: var(--muted); }
.meter { height: 8px; border-radius: 99px; background: var(--line); overflow: hidden; }
.meter span { display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--accent); }
.compact .v { font-size: 18px; }

JavaScript

const darkQuery = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');
const wideQuery = matchMedia('(min-width: 560px)');
const buttons = document.querySelectorAll('[data-choice]');
let choice = localStorage.getItem('theme') ?? 'system';

function applyTheme() {
  const dark = choice === 'dark' || (choice === 'system' && darkQuery.matches);
  document.documentElement.dataset.theme = dark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  buttons.forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.dataset.choice === choice));
  document.querySelector('#sys').textContent = darkQuery.matches ? '🌙 Dark' : '☀️ Light';
}

function applyLayout() {
  document.body.classList.toggle('compact', !wideQuery.matches);
  document.querySelector('#bp').textContent =
    wideQuery.matches ? 'Layout: wide (≥ 560px)' : 'Layout: compact (< 560px)';
}

document.querySelector('.seg').addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const btn = event.target.closest('[data-choice]');
  if (!btn) return;
  choice = btn.dataset.choice;
  localStorage.setItem('theme', choice);
  applyTheme();
  console.log('Theme choice:', choice);
});

// Live updates: the OS theme or the window width changes
darkQuery.addEventListener('change', applyTheme);
wideQuery.addEventListener('change', applyLayout);
applyTheme();
applyLayout();
console.log('System dark?', darkQuery.matches, '| saved choice:', choice);

Pick System, Light or Dark. On System the page follows your OS setting live; the choice survives a rerun because it is in localStorage.

Watch out: the old mql.addListener() is deprecated. Use mql.addEventListener('change', fn).

Network state and Page Visibility

navigator.onLine and the online/offline events on window tell you when the device loses its network. Only false is fully trustworthy: true means “connected to something”, such as café Wi-Fi with no internet. So use the events to show a banner and queue changes, but still handle failed fetch calls.

The Page Visibility API tells you whether the user can see the tab. document.visibilityState is 'visible' or 'hidden', and visibilitychange fires on document when it changes. Use it to pause videos, carousels and polling, and to stop counting “time on page”. Browsers throttle timers in hidden tabs heavily, so a setInterval clock drifts when the tab is in the background; pausing and resuming on visibility keeps your numbers honest. It is also the most reliable moment to send final analytics with navigator.sendBeacon(), because unload often never fires on mobile.

Try it: Online, offline and tab visibility

HTML

<main class="app">
  <div id="banner" class="banner" role="status" hidden>You are offline. Changes are saved on this device and will sync later.</div>
  <header class="head">
    <h1>Class notes</h1>
    <span id="net" class="badge">Online</span>
  </header>
  <form id="form" class="row">
    <input id="note" placeholder="Write a note and press Save" aria-label="Note" required>
    <button class="btn">Save</button>
  </form>
  <ul id="list" class="list"></ul>
  <footer class="foot">
    <span>Queued: <b id="queued">0</b></span>
    <span>Time on page: <b id="time">0s</b></span>
    <button type="button" class="chip" data-sim="offline">Simulate offline</button>
    <button type="button" class="chip" data-sim="online">Simulate online</button>
  </footer>
</main>

CSS

:root { --accent: #2563eb; --line: #e5e7eb; }
body { margin: 0; background: #f8fafc; }
.app { max-width: 600px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; }
.banner { background: #fff7ed; color: #9a3412; border: 1px solid #fed7aa;
  border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px 12px; font-size: 14px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
.head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; }
h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
.badge { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 99px;
  background: #dcfce7; color: #166534; }
.badge.off { background: #fee2e2; color: #991b1b; }
.row { display: flex; gap: 8px; }
.row input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; font: inherit; padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; background: #fff; }
.row input:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); border-color: transparent; }
.btn { font: inherit; font-weight: 600; border: 0; border-radius: 10px;
  padding: 10px 16px; background: var(--accent); color: #fff; cursor: pointer; }
.list { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 12px 0; display: grid; gap: 8px; }
.list li { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; background: #fff;
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 12px; font-size: 14px; }
.list small { color: #6b7280; white-space: nowrap; }
.list .pending small { color: #c2410c; }
.foot { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px 16px; align-items: center;
  font-size: 13px; color: #475569; }
.chip { font: inherit; font-size: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--line);
  background: #fff; border-radius: 99px; padding: 4px 10px; cursor: pointer; }

JavaScript

const list = document.querySelector('#list');
const net = document.querySelector('#net');
const banner = document.querySelector('#banner');
let online = navigator.onLine; // only "false" is fully trustworthy
const queue = [];

function addNote(text, pending) {
  const li = document.createElement('li');
  li.className = pending ? 'pending' : '';
  const span = document.createElement('span');
  span.textContent = text;
  const small = document.createElement('small');
  small.textContent = pending ? 'Waiting to sync' : 'Synced';
  li.append(span, small);
  list.prepend(li);
  return li;
}

function renderStatus() {
  net.textContent = online ? 'Online' : 'Offline';
  net.classList.toggle('off', !online);
  banner.hidden = online;
  document.querySelector('#queued').textContent = queue.length;
}

document.querySelector('#form').addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const input = document.querySelector('#note');
  const li = addNote(input.value, !online);
  if (!online) queue.push(li);
  input.value = '';
  renderStatus();
});

function handleNetwork(event) {
  online = event.type === 'online';
  console.log('Network event:', event.type);
  if (online) {
    for (const li of queue.splice(0)) {
      li.className = '';
      li.lastChild.textContent = 'Synced';
    }
  }
  renderStatus();
}
addEventListener('online', handleNetwork);
addEventListener('offline', handleNetwork);

// The buttons only simulate: they dispatch the same events the browser fires
document.querySelector('.foot').addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const type = event.target.dataset.sim;
  if (type) dispatchEvent(new Event(type));
});

// Page Visibility: count only the time the tab is actually visible
let seconds = 0;
setInterval(() => {
  if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') {
    seconds += 1;
    document.querySelector('#time').textContent = seconds + 's';
  }
}, 1000);
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
  console.log('Tab is now', document.visibilityState, 'at', seconds + 's');
});

addNote('Revise closures before Friday', false);
renderStatus();
console.log('Started', online ? 'online' : 'offline', '|', document.visibilityState);

You cannot unplug the playground, so the Simulate buttons dispatch real offline/online events. Switch to another browser tab and back to see the visibility log.

Notifications and permissions (code only)

Notifications show a system pop-up even when your tab is in the background. The permission has three states: 'default' (not asked yet), 'granted' and 'denied'. Once denied, you cannot ask again from code: the user must change it in site settings. That is why you ask in context, from a click on something like “Deal alerts”, never on page load.

alertsBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (!('Notification' in window)) return say('Not supported here');
  if (Notification.permission === 'denied') {
    return say('Alerts are blocked. Enable them in site settings.');
  }
  const result = await Notification.requestPermission();
  if (result === 'granted') {
    new Notification('Ralfiz Store', { body: 'We will ping you when prices drop.' });
  }
});

On Android Chrome, new Notification() throws: mobile notifications must come from a service worker with registration.showNotification(). Real push notifications (sent from your server while the site is closed) also need a service worker and the Push API, which is beyond this lesson.

Geolocation (code only)

navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(success, error, options) uses callbacks, not promises. The error object has a code: 1 is permission denied, 2 is position unavailable, 3 is timeout. Options include enableHighAccuracy, timeout in milliseconds and maximumAge for a cached position. Wrap it in a promise so you can await it:

function getPosition(options = { timeout: 8000, maximumAge: 60000 }) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (!('geolocation' in navigator)) {
      return reject(new Error('Geolocation not supported'));
    }
    navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(resolve, reject, options);
  });
}

findBtn.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  try {
    const { coords } = await getPosition();
    showNearestStore(coords.latitude, coords.longitude);
  } catch (err) {
    const reasons = { 1: 'Location blocked', 2: 'Location unavailable', 3: 'Timed out' };
    say(reasons[err.code] ?? err.message);
    showStorePicker(); // always offer a manual fallback
  }
});

watchPosition() keeps reporting as the user moves (for delivery tracking) and returns an id you pass to clearWatch(). Location is personal data: ask only when needed, explain why, and never send it to your server without saying so.

Example: Ralfiz Deals page

The lab builds one promo page that uses everything above, in the order a real team would add it:

  1. Coupon card. copyText() tries the Clipboard API and falls back to selecting the input. The status line has role="status" so screen readers hear “Code copied”.
  2. Share. Web Share when available, otherwise copy the deal URL. AbortError is ignored.
  3. Theme. System, Light and Dark buttons with aria-pressed. The theme is derived from the saved choice and prefers-color-scheme, and updates live.
  4. Offline banner. The Claim button is disabled while offline, and a banner explains why.
  5. Countdown. The “deal ends in” timer computes the remaining time from an end date on every tick, so throttling in background tabs cannot make it wrong, and it skips DOM updates while the tab is hidden.
  6. Store finder and alerts. Geolocation and Notifications run only from their buttons, with every failure path handled.

Test it in Chrome DevTools: the Network panel has an Offline preset, the Rendering panel can emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark, and the Sensors panel can fake a location.

Common mistakes

1. Assuming an API exists. This crashes in browsers without Web Share:

shareBtn.onclick = () => navigator.share(data); // TypeError on some desktops

Fix: detect first and keep a fallback.

shareBtn.hidden = typeof navigator.share !== 'function';
copyLinkBtn.hidden = !shareBtn.hidden;

2. Saying “Copied” before the promise settles.

navigator.clipboard.writeText(code);
label.textContent = 'Copied!'; // shown even when it failed

Fix: await it inside try, and show the success message only after it resolves.

3. Asking for permissions on page load.

Notification.requestPermission(); // top of app.js: blocked or denied

Fix: call it inside a click handler for a feature the user just asked for.

4. Reading matches once. if (matchMedia(q).matches) setDark(); never updates. Fix: keep the MediaQueryList and add a change listener.

5. Trusting timers in background tabs. A countdown that does remaining -= 1 every second drifts when the tab is hidden. Fix: compute endTime - Date.now() on each tick.

Interview and real-world notes

  • Explain the gates: secure context, user activation, permission, and Permissions Policy for iframes. That shows you understand why an API fails, not just that it does.
  • “Progressive enhancement with feature detection” is the phrase interviewers want when they ask how you support many browsers.
  • navigator.onLine === true does not mean the API is reachable. Mention offline queues and retry.
  • Use visibilitychange (not unload) for last-moment analytics with sendBeacon.
  • Permissions are a product decision: explain before you ask, ask in context, and design a path for “denied”.
  • New APIs appear every year. Check MDN and caniuse.com before you depend on one, and read its “Secure context” and “Permissions Policy” notes.

terms.definition: A page served over HTTPS or from localhost. Powerful APIs such as the Clipboard, Web Share, Geolocation and Notifications only work there. Check with window.isSecureContext.
A recent click, tap or key press by the user. Some APIs (share, clipboard write in Safari and Firefox, notification prompts in most browsers) refuse to run without it.
Checking that an API exists before using it, for example if (navigator.share), and giving a fallback when it does not.
navigator.permissions.query({name}) reports whether a permission is granted, denied or prompt, without triggering a prompt.
The object returned by matchMedia(query). Its matches property is true or false and it fires a change event when the answer changes.
document.visibilityState is visible or hidden; the visibilitychange event fires when the user switches tabs or minimises the window.
A rule, set by HTTP header or an iframe allow attribute, that decides which features a page or frame may use at all, such as clipboard-write or geolocation.

lessons.examTip: In interviews, say “feature-detect, then progressively enhance”: the basic page works everywhere, and APIs like Web Share only add a better path where they exist.

quiz.question: Your Share button works on phones but a desktop tester reports it does nothing and the console shows TypeError: navigator.share is not a function. What is the right fix?
options: Wrap the call in try/catch and ignore the error
Feature-detect navigator.share and show a Copy link fallback when it is missing
Ask the user to install a browser extension
Call navigator.share inside setTimeout so it loads first
quiz.explanation: Web Share is not available in every desktop browser. Check that navigator.share exists and offer a fallback such as copying the link; try/catch alone leaves the user with a dead button.

quiz.question: Why does calling Notification.requestPermission() as soon as the page loads usually fail or annoy users?
options: It only works on localhost
It needs a service worker first
Browsers expect it to be triggered by a user gesture, and an unexplained prompt on load is often blocked or denied
It can only be called once per browser session
quiz.explanation: Browsers increasingly require a user gesture for permission prompts and may quietly block prompts on load. Ask in context, after the user clicks something like Deal alerts, so they understand why.

quiz.question: navigator.onLine is true. What do you know for sure?
options: The device is connected to some network, but not that the internet or your API is reachable
Your API server is up
The last fetch succeeded
The user has a fast connection
quiz.explanation: onLine is only reliable when it is false. True means there is a network connection, which may be a Wi-Fi without internet. Always handle fetch failures too.

quiz.question: Which code keeps a theme in sync when the user switches their operating system to dark mode while the page is open?
options: Read matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches once on load
Poll window.innerWidth every second
Listen for the storage event
Keep the MediaQueryList and listen to its change event
quiz.explanation: matches is a snapshot. The MediaQueryList fires change whenever the result flips, so store it and call addEventListener('change', …) to re-apply the theme.
